title: Penicillin is first given to a patient in Oxford
summary: At the Radcliffe Infirmary, police constable Albert Alexander, dying of a severe infection, became the first patient treated with purified penicillin. He improved dramatically, but supplies ran out and he died weeks later.
reason: Howard Florey and Ernst Chain's team had turned Alexander Fleming's 1928 discovery into a usable drug, but could make only tiny amounts.
significance: It showed penicillin worked in people and led to the mass production that saved countless lives by the war's end.
